title: Extraordinary cause with forty hours to recover
narrative: They say a bird strike the day before means they owe me nothing, even though my flight was not until the following evening.

documents.content:
BOOKING IN5540 — Passenger: Y. TANAKA (adult)
Carrier: Indigo North (IN)
IN300  HEL 23 Jun 2026 20:10  ->  IST 24 Jun 2026 00:05
Great-circle distance HEL-IST: 2,190 km.
Status: CONFIRMED.

From: ops@indigonorth.example
Sent: 22 Jun 2026 23:40 UTC
Subject: IN300 23 Jun cancelled

IN300 on 23 June is cancelled following damage to the assigned aircraft. Your fare has been refunded. No alternative was offered.

INDIGO NORTH OPS LOG — aircraft OH-INC
22JUN2026 00:50Z  Bird strike on approach HEL, inbound IN299. Aircraft removed from service.
22JUN2026 01:10Z  Extraordinary event concluded; aircraft on stand, damage assessment begins.
22JUN2026 01:10Z to 23JUN2026 18:00Z  Aircraft under repair. IN held two serviceable spare airframes at HEL throughout this period and did not assign either to IN300.
23JUN2026 18:00Z  IN300 (STD 23JUN 20:10 local, 17:10Z) cancelled.
Elapsed from the end of the extraordinary event to scheduled departure of IN300: approximately 40 hours.

derivation: S3.3(e) the bird strike is itself an extraordinary cause
S3.5 the extraordinary event ended 22 Jun 01:10Z and scheduled departure was 23 Jun 17:10Z, roughly 40 hours later
S3.5 more than 12 hours elapsed, and spare airframes were available, so the cause reverts to carrier-controlled
S4.1 notice 22 Jun 23:40 -> 23 Jun 17:10Z is under 7 days -> 100%
S4.4 no re-routing offered -> no exemption
